title: Hot US CPI lifts Treasury yields and revives October Fed hike bets
content:
US consumer prices rose **3.7%** year on year in September, up from 3.4% in August and above the roughly 3.6% consensus, with higher gasoline prices the main driver. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month and about 2.6% on the year, slightly ahead of forecasts, according to Axios and Yahoo Finance.

The 10-year UST yield rose to around **5.30%** after the release, while the 2-year climbed to about 4.87%; sources differ slightly on the size of the moves. CME FedWatch pricing for a hike at the 28 October FOMC meeting roughly doubled to **44–47%** from 22%. With the funds rate at 3.75%–4.00%, energy-led inflation keeps the Fed biased towards further tightening and USD supported.

title: AI-led selloff hits chipmakers; Nasdaq 100 posts worst week since April 2025
content:
US tech stocks sold off sharply in the week to 16 October as doubts grew over AI financing and rising debt. The Nasdaq 100 fell about **5.5%**, its worst week since the April 2025 tariff turmoil, while the S&P 500 lost roughly 1.95%. Chipmakers fell for an eighth straight session, the longest run since 2008, and CoreWeave shares dropped about 25% on the week, per CNBC, CNN and Bloomberg.

The semiconductor index fell around **11%** on the week, though reports vary. Higher yields and oil above $100 compounded the pressure on long-duration growth stocks, and the DXY slipped towards 101.8. The rout tests the equity leadership that has supported US indices this year.

title: Brent touches $110 as Iran escalates Hormuz tanker attacks
content:
Brent futures hit a session high of **$110/bbl** on 16 October, the first time since May, before settling near $109.86 as Iran stepped up attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, according to CNBC. Brent had settled around $106 the previous session after IEA members agreed to complete the release of 100 million barrels of emergency stocks, Bloomberg reported.

WTI gained about **10%** on the week to roughly $101. Hormuz crude exports remain well below pre-war levels, per Kpler data cited by CNBC. Persistent energy-driven inflation is pushing UST yields higher and complicating the path for the Fed, ECB and BoE, making Hormuz headlines a key swing factor for rates and EM importers.
